See under Behçet’s syndrome, above and under HIV-associated complications, above. Oesophageal ulceration. Thalidomide has been shown to be of benefit in the treatment of idiopathic oesophageal ulcers in pa- tients with AIDS (see under HIV-associated complications, above). Thalidomide has also been reported to have healed an oesophageal ulcer refractory to other treatments in an immuno- competent patient,1 and in an immunocompromised patient after liver transplant.2 1.
